prompt.brief: Design Instagram for hundreds of millions of daily users: people upload photos and videos, follow accounts, read a personalized feed, publish expiring stories, and receive media and interaction updates reliably.
successSignals: Separate durable media metadata and social graph state from object storage, CDN delivery, and rebuildable feed projections.
Choose fanout-on-write, fanout-on-read, or a hybrid strategy for normal and celebrity accounts.
Design resumable uploads, asynchronous processing, privacy and moderation checks, and idempotent interaction events.
Bound feed reads and story expiry work while making freshness, deletion, and regional failure behavior explicit.

functional: Upload photos and videos, generate multiple renditions, and publish a post or 24-hour story.
Follow and unfollow users, read a personalized feed, and view a profile timeline.
Like, comment, share, and receive notifications for eligible interactions.
Search users and hashtags while enforcing private accounts, blocks, moderation, deletion, and data export rules.
nonFunctional: A post's metadata and ownership must be durable before publication; media processing may complete asynchronously.
Target p95 under 200 ms for a cached feed page and under 2 seconds for normal media availability after upload.
Serve popular media through a CDN, isolate celebrity fanout, and avoid blocking reads on recommendation or moderation workers.
Tolerate resumable upload retries, worker failures, duplicate events, story expiry races, and regional degradation.
scaleAssumptions: 500 million daily active users, 100 million media uploads per day, and 10 million concurrent feed or story viewers at peak.
Most users follow fewer than 1,000 accounts; a small number of creators have tens of millions of followers.
Each upload produces several image or video renditions; originals and derivatives are stored in object storage with lifecycle tiers.
Stories expire after 24 hours, but deletion and privacy changes must invalidate them immediately from serving paths.

metrics.label: Media upload rate
metrics.description: 100M uploads per day; provision ingestion, object storage, and processing for event bursts.

metrics.label: Feed read latency
metrics.description: Serve a bounded cursor page from projections and cache without scanning the social graph.

metrics.label: Media readiness
metrics.description: Upload acknowledgement is immediate; normal renditions become playable asynchronously within this target.

metrics.label: Story lifetime
metrics.description: TTL is a serving rule, backed by durable state and explicit deletion or moderation invalidation.

entities.name: MediaAsset
entities.notes: Store bytes in object storage and metadata separately; checksums and immutable versions make retries safe.

entities.name: PostOrStory
entities.notes: A story is a content record with an expiry policy; visibility and moderation are rechecked at read time.

entities.name: FollowEdge
entities.notes: Maintain follower and following access paths to support feed fanout, profile views, blocks, and privacy checks.

entities.name: FeedEntry
entities.notes: A rebuildable read projection with bounded retention; hot creators can be merged on read instead of pushed to every follower.

entities.name: InteractionEvent
entities.notes: At-least-once events drive counters, notifications, moderation signals, and analytics with consumer deduplication.

apis.contract: { contentType, size, checksum, requestId } -> { uploadId, partUrls }
apis.notes: Authorize ownership, issue signed resumable part URLs, and do not proxy large bytes through the API tier.

apis.contract: { uploadId, caption, visibility, requestId } -> { postId, state }
apis.notes: Validate the completed asset, persist metadata idempotently, and enqueue processing and publication events.
Read a bounded projection, merge hot-author candidates when needed, and recheck visibility, block, and moderation state.
Return only unexpired, visible stories; cache short-lived manifests and invalidate on deletion or moderation.
Use a unique actor-content key and an idempotent event so repeated taps cannot duplicate interactions.

dataFlow.title: Reserve a resumable upload
dataFlow.description: The client requests a signed multipart upload, sends bytes directly to object storage, and retries failed parts by checksum.

dataFlow.title: Commit content metadata
dataFlow.description: After storage confirms the object, the API validates ownership and moderation policy, writes the post or story record, and returns a durable content ID.

dataFlow.title: Process media asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Workers scan, resize, transcode, and create manifests and thumbnails; the content becomes playable when the required rendition set is ready.

dataFlow.title: Fan out eligible feed entries
dataFlow.description: A publication event selects push fanout for normal authors and pull-on-read or hybrid delivery for high-follower creators, applying visibility and block rules.

dataFlow.title: Serve and invalidate asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Feed and story reads use cursor projections, CDN media, and freshness metadata while counters, notifications, recommendations, analytics, and expiry cleanup consume events independently.

architecture.title: Instagram reference architecture
architecture.summary: Clients upload directly to object storage, while durable content and graph services publish events to media workers, hybrid feed fanout, CDN manifests, and interaction consumers.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Clients upload media, browse feeds and stories, and submit interactions.

layers.label: Source and graph layer
layers.description: Durable content, media metadata, ownership, visibility, and social relationships.

layers.label: Media and feed plane
layers.description: Asynchronous processing, object delivery, and hybrid feed projections.

layers.label: Extensions and operations
layers.description: Notifications, moderation, ranking, analytics, expiry, and observability consume events independently.

keyPaths.label: Upload and publish path
keyPaths.description: Client -> signed object upload -> content service -> durable metadata -> media workers.

keyPaths.label: Feed read path
keyPaths.description: Client -> feed service -> projection/cache, with hot-author merge and CDN media URLs.

keyPaths.label: Hybrid publication path
keyPaths.description: Content event -> fanout strategy -> follower projections or pull-on-read.

deepDives.title: Media uploads and delivery
points: Use direct resumable multipart uploads with checksums so retries do not resend large payloads through application servers.
Store originals and immutable renditions in object storage; publish only after required processing and moderation state is known.
Use signed CDN URLs, cache keys by rendition/version, and invalidation or tombstones for deletion and privacy changes.

deepDives.title: Feed fanout and celebrity accounts
points: Push feed entries for ordinary authors because most home reads should be bounded and cheap.
Pull recent posts for celebrity accounts because writing to millions of followers per upload creates a burst; merge a bounded number of pull sources on read.
Use separate queues, shard fanout, and backpressure so a viral account cannot starve normal publication work.

deepDives.title: Stories, deletion, and privacy
points: Represent story expiry as durable content state plus a serving TTL; cleanup is asynchronous but reads must reject expired content immediately.
Recheck visibility, blocks, moderation, and deletion at read time because a projection may outlive a policy change.
Emit tombstones to invalidate feed entries, CDN manifests, counters, notifications, and analytics copies according to deletion policy.

deepDives.title: Interactions and ranking
points: Use actor-content uniqueness and idempotent events for likes, comments, and shares under retries and rapid taps.
Keep interaction counts and recommendation features as projections that can be rebuilt from retained events.
Introduce personalized ranking after the chronological or bounded feed path is correct; version candidates and ranking models for explainability.

tradeoffs.title: Fanout on write versus read
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use hybrid fanout: push ordinary authors and pull high-follower accounts, with a configurable threshold.
tradeoffs.caution: Pure push amplifies celebrity writes; pure pull makes every feed read traverse too much graph and increases tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Original quality versus delivery cost
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep originals for durable ownership and generate bounded renditions for device and bandwidth classes at the edge.
tradeoffs.caution: Serving originals everywhere increases egress and startup cost; generating every possible rendition wastes storage and processing.

tradeoffs.title: Strong versus eventual interaction counts
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly commit the actor's interaction state and use versioned eventual counters for high-volume display reads.
tradeoffs.caution: An exact aggregate read across all interactions is too expensive for hot content, but stale counts need freshness metadata.

commonMistakes: Proxying all media through the API servers instead of using signed direct uploads and CDN delivery.
Faning out every post synchronously to every follower, ignoring celebrity accounts and backpressure.
Treating feed entries, story TTLs, counters, or CDN objects as the source of truth.
Ignoring duplicate uploads, retries, moderation, privacy, deletion, and blocked users.
Adding ranking or recommendation complexity before defining a bounded, observable feed contract.

followUps.question: How would you support a private account?
followUps.answer: Store visibility and follow approval durably, authorize feed and media URL issuance, and recheck access on reads so cached projections cannot leak content.

followUps.question: What happens when media processing is delayed?
followUps.answer: Persist the post as processing, show a safe placeholder and progress state, retry through a queue, and publish the feed entry only when the required rendition policy is met.

followUps.question: How would you rebuild a user's feed?
followUps.answer: Replay follow, post, moderation, deletion, and ranking events into a shadow projection, compare versions, then replace the bounded user partition incrementally.

followUps.question: How do you handle a viral creator?
followUps.answer: Use pull-on-read or hybrid delivery, isolate the creator's event and fanout partitions, cache recent content and renditions, and send refresh hints rather than pushing full feeds.

rubric.description: Direct resumable upload, object storage, processing, signed CDN delivery, lifecycle, and deletion invalidation are explicit.
The answer explains bounded cursor reads, hybrid fanout, celebrity isolation, cache behavior, and freshness.
Durable metadata, idempotent interactions, privacy, moderation, expiry, deletion, and projection rebuilds are covered.
The design accounts for upload bursts, large media, follower skew, CDN egress, worker queues, and regional failures.
Notifications, search, recommendations, ranking, and analytics remain asynchronous and independently versioned.
